# QuietFollow Positioning

All statements below are synthetic input facts, hypotheses, or explicit unknowns. They
are not external research or measured product evidence.

## Segment

- Evidence class: synthetic owner brief.
- Input fact: solo consultants who promise personal follow-ups after client conversations
  and currently review notes manually.

## Category and context

- Evidence class: synthetic product definition.
- Input fact: local personal follow-up tracker, not a CRM or outbound communication platform.

## Alternatives and substitutes

| Alternative | Evidence class | Input fact |
|---|---|---|
| Spreadsheet | Synthetic fixture comparison | Flexible and familiar; manual due filtering and outcome history are easy to miss. |
| Generic task app | Synthetic fixture comparison | Strong reminders; contact context and repeated follow-up history are fragmented. |
| CRM | Synthetic fixture comparison | Rich pipeline and automation; setup and operating overhead are disproportionate for one consultant. |

## Differentiated value hypothesis

- Evidence class: hypothesis.
- Input fact: one minimal loop connecting contact, due date, due view, and outcome.

## Known evidence

- Only the synthetic owner brief and fixture comparison.
- No interviews, analytics, pricing study, or demand measurement exist.

## Strong unknowns

- Reachable segment.
- Willingness to switch or pay.
- Acceptable operating burden.
- Whether the focused loop beats a task app.

## Non-goals

- Email sending, payment, analytics, public deployment, team workflows, real customer
  data, and automatic CRM import.
